sentences.text: Cathartesaura was a medium-sized herbivore featuring a long, lightly built, and well-muscled neck that allowed only limited vertical movement.
This dinosaur is distinguished by unique vertebral features, such as bony laminae associations and pneumatic chambers in the neck, which link it to the family Rebbachisauridae.
The genus name Cathartesaura combines the New World vulture genus Cathartes with the Greek word for lizard.
The species name anaerobica honors the Argentinian adhesive company Anaeróbicos for supporting the fossil extraction and preparation.
Gallina and Apesteguía described Cathartesaura in 2005 based on a partial skeleton containing vertebrae and limb bones.
Cathartesaura is a member of the class Saurischia.
It is classified in the family Rebbachisauridae.
The dinosaur belongs to the subfamily Limaysaurinae.
Cathartesaura lived between 110.1 and 106.3 million years ago during the Albian stage.
It inhabited the Huincul Formation of the Neuquén Basin in Río Negro Province, Argentina.
Fossils were found in mudstone and sandstone layers dating to the Albian stage at the base of the formation.

Its discovery alongside other rebbachisaurids, the only diplodocoid group in the early Late Cretaceous, supports the idea that an extinction event eliminated diplodocoids, allowing saltasaurine titanosaurs to fill their niche.
